prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: native pixel-art afraid eye atlas for an NPC portrait
Input images: the single attached local candidate eye reference grid. It is the exact original upper-half face crop, face identity and palette reference.

Create one exact 2×2 atlas. Each cell is the same complete 64:35 upper-half crop, with no labels, borders, gutters, margins, text, extra panels or decoration. Required row-major order: top-left OPEN; top-right HALF-CLOSED; bottom-left FULLY-CLOSED; bottom-right OPEN REPEAT. Preserve identical framing and pixel registration in every cell.

Expression: NPC073 afraid, with tense lifted inner brows and alert lids. The face must read fearful rather than neutral or merely round surprised. Keep both brows visibly tense and raised, but restrained and consistent across all four cells. Preserve the original face, eye spacing, nose bridge, hair/silhouette and warm muted palette.

Keep each olive-brown iris and pupil compact, natural and fully inside the source eye aperture. Do not make round surprised disks, enlarge or stretch irises, expose broad white sclera, move the pupils outside their lids, or add bright glints. Open phases are alert but controlled. The half-closed phase follows the open iris placement and geometry under naturally lowered lids; no fixed slit detached from the eyes. The fully closed phase has continuous opaque lids covering iris and sclera while retaining the same fearful brow expression. OPEN REPEAT should match the top-left open pose.

Keep soft native pixel clusters, original muted skin/hair tones, full upper-half crop and exact image scale. No face-shape or hair changes, blur, smoothing, antialiasing, vector circles, gradients, harsh dark outlines, oversized eyes or new background details.
